title: SST-product errors go into SOCAT fCO2 temperature recalculations: with DOISST v2.1 the 1995-2024 ocean CO2 sink trend is 0.15 PgC/yr per decade smaller than with CCI v3
abstract:
Recent ocean CO2 sink estimates recalculate each SOCAT fCO2 value from the ship intake temperature to a satellite SST (DOISST in Watson et al. 2020; ESA CCI SST v3 in Ford et al. 2026 and two GCB2025 products). fCO2 changes by 4.23% per kelvin, so time-dependent SST errors become sink errors. We reduced 44 million SOCATv2026 rows to 2.2 million daily super-observations and compared DOISST v2.1 and CCI v3 with the intake temperature of the same platform (288 open-ocean ships, moorings and autonomous platforms, 1995-2024, platform fixed effects, bootstrap, placebo dates). We added HadSST4.2 (50 ensemble members) as an independent reference and SeaFlux fields to convert temperature errors to PgC/yr.

At the SOCAT sites, DOISST minus CCI v3 increases by 0.042 C per decade (95% interval 0.024-0.060). Thus a DOISST-based recalculation gives a sink trend 0.15 PgC/yr per decade (0.08-0.21) smaller than a CCI-based one. DOISST has a step on 7 July 2020: +0.067 C (0.018-0.112) against SOCAT intake temperatures with daily DOISST, +0.057 C against HadSST4.2 and +0.05-0.07 C against CCI v3. This makes a DOISST-based sink 0.19-0.25 PgC/yr smaller from mid-2020. CCI v3 has no step then. The 2005 DOISST step is small at the SOCAT sites.

The references disagree on which product drifts. Against HadSST4.2, DOISST warms 0.057 C per decade and CCI v3 is stable (-0.007). Against SOCAT platforms, DOISST warms 0.019 and CCI v3 cools 0.024 C per decade, mostly by a -0.04 C change in 2015-2016 that HadSST4.2 does not show. Limitations: no fCO2 mapping was run (an ocean-wide sensitivity of 0.35 PgC/yr per 0.1 C was used), the in situ references are uncertain, and the ship-only 2020 step is not significant.
